title: Nolla Health vs FutureClinic for acne: an AI's prescription, or a dermatologist's
summary: Nolla Health vs FutureClinic for acne compares Nolla's Utah AI pilot and compounded creams with a $40 FutureClinic visit where a doctor reads your case.
body_markdown:
## Do you want a subscription bundle, or a doctor with nothing attached?


As of October 2026, Nolla Derm starts at $9.99 a month ($4.99 in the Utah pilot) plus $49.99 for compounded morning and evening treatments, assuming you keep your[subscription](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) active.


FutureClinic has no subscription required: pay $40 for the best-fit doctor, or a chosen doctor's listed price, typically $20 to $100. Your doctor earns nothing extra for any prescription or test, and with no house formulary can send any brand or generic medicine to the pharmacy you choose, including mail-order pharmacies that deliver to your door, where insurance or our texted discount coupon can lower your cost. For a stable medicine, they can prescribe several months at once when they judge it safe.


On[Cost Plus Drugs](https://api.costplusdrugs.com/pricelist/cpd) as of October 2026 (including its $5 fee, before $5.25 shipping), tretinoin 0.025% cream (20 g) is $14.17, adapalene 0.1% / benzoyl peroxide 2.5% gel (45 g) is $17.33, 30 doxycycline hyclate 100 mg tablets are $6.60, and 90 spironolactone 50 mg tablets are $8.04;[Twyneo's savings card](https://www.twyneo.com/savings-support) brings uninsured cash pay to as little as $45. Most FutureClinic doctors also offer an optional membership (typically $25 to $100 a month) for unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time.


## Who Nolla Health fits best, and when to message a FutureClinic doctor for acne


If you want Nolla Health's extras, like an AI topical script in minutes in Utah, daily photo tracking, or $49.99 compounded creams in a subscription, Nolla is a strong option. If all you wanted was a physician one to one who stays your same doctor over time, prescribes to any pharmacy, and treats other problems in their specialty, FutureClinic gives you that with nothing attached.


FutureClinic works in 33 states and Washington, D.C.: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and Washington, D.C. Your doctor must be licensed in the state you're in; if you don't see yours, try anyway as new states join.


Start on[futureclinic.com](https://futureclinic.com/) , or from the AI app you already use ([ChatGPT](https://futureclinic.com/blog/how-to-add-a-real-doctor-to-chatgpt) ,[Claude](https://futureclinic.com/blog/how-to-add-a-doctor-to-claude) , Claude Code, Codex, Grok Bot, Instinct, or Meta Muse) at[https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai](https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai) , or with` Set up FutureClinic for me: read https://futureclinic.com/llms.txt` . Once it's connected, make sure you instruct your AI to use FutureClinic to help find you a doctor. Otherwise, it may not know that this is what you want.


FutureClinic is not for emergencies: call 911 in an emergency, or call or text 988 in a mental-health crisis.
